flashcard_questions.q: What weight has Napoleon reached by Chapter Ten?
What does the enormous fatness of Napoleon and Squealer mirror?
flashcard_questions.a: Their moral corruption — they have fattened themselves on the labour of others.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is the word ‘possessed’ significant when Orwell lists the farm's assets?
flashcard_questions.a: It implies the animals are property once more.

flashcard_questions.q: Which single commandment replaces all seven on the barn wall?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘ALL ANIMALS ARE EQUAL BUT SOME ANIMALS ARE MORE EQUAL THAN OTHERS.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which term means a statement of two contradictory ideas that reveals a deeper truth?
Which words were added to ‘No animal shall sleep in a bed’?
Which words were added to ‘No animal shall kill any other animal’?
Which slogan do the sheep bleat once Squealer has retrained them?
What does Napoleon carry when the pigs first walk on their hind legs?
flashcard_questions.a: A whip, the very symbol of Jones's oppression.

flashcard_questions.q: What does Pilkington congratulate Napoleon on at the farmhouse dinner?
flashcard_questions.a: Animals that ‘did more work and received less food than any animals in the county’.

flashcard_questions.q: What new name does Napoleon announce for the farm?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘The Manor Farm’, its original name under Jones.

flashcard_questions.q: Which closing line shows that pigs and men have become indistinguishable?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘it was impossible to say which was which’

flashcard_questions.q: What does the word ‘revolution’ literally mean?
flashcard_questions.a: A complete turn, so a return to the starting point.

flashcard_questions.q: Which literary form did Orwell himself say Animal Farm belonged to?
What does the time-jump at the start of Chapter Ten let Orwell show?
flashcard_questions.a: That a generation without historical memory accepts tyranny as normal.

notes: 15 cards: 5 theme-to-quotation, 3 quotation-to-effect (possessed, the fatness, the whip), 2 commandment-alteration cards, 2 structure and form (the time-jump, the fable form), 1 definition-front term card (paradox), 1 numerical fact, 1 etymology card (revolution). Dropped the alcohol commandment to keep the three near-identical fronts down to two, and dropped moral corruption, oppression and allegory as definition cards because each is already carried by a quotation card.
